MANIFEST rev 3 on main at ab274f2 (bd-01M15R1K434JHHJWKNGHTYKDP3, docs-only, one file, rv-01M15RM1KMQWDEYHHT8H38B78W). This is the consequence rev 2 created: I wrote a rule that disqualifies famous stories from the partition that decides defaults, and my own list had five of them. Fixing the doc rather than leaving the rule pointing at unfixed selections.

1. THE SCORE IS MEASURED, NOT GUESSED. My intuition about "how famous is this story" has no business in a freeze receipt. Rev 3 gives a reproducible procedure: count dedicated summary surfaces for the exact title+author across a FROZEN site list (SparkNotes, CliffsNotes, Shmoop, LitCharts, GradeSaver, Wikipedia plot section, Course Hero, eNotes); high = a plot summary on 3 or more, or a Wikipedia article with a plot section; medium = 1-2; low = none; record count, date and the site list, re-check on re-freeze. And I say in the doc what the proxy is NOT: it measures how much summary text about a story sits on the open web, not whether any given provider trained on it. That is exactly why the fame-by-channel leakage control is the real defence and the score is only triage.

2. REPLACEMENTS THAT KEEP THE PHENOMENON. A story is in the set because of a phenomenon, so swapping for obscurity alone would trade one bias for a worse one - an obscure story that stresses nothing is not an improvement. Each replacement is same-author, same-device: Saki's Open Window -> another Beasts and Super-Beasts story with the same unreliable-embedded-report device; Bierce's Owl Creek -> The Boarded Window or One of the Missing (same volume, retrospective flashback and subjective time, without the fame); Gift of the Magi -> a lesser story from the same 1906 collection; Story of an Hour -> another Chopin belief-vs-fact reversal; To Build a Fire -> Love of Life for the long low-dialogue sensory slot. All PD bases still marked verify; nothing is fetched.

3. A GAP I AM PUTTING ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN QUIETLY LEAVING. After the swaps, set 1 still has essentially no story with genuine discourse-level ANACHRONY except the Bierce replacement. Our model is partial, unbalanced, hierarchical alignment with omission, merge, split, REORDER, revisit and external destinations, and the vision asks in as many words whether recall followed presentation order, story-world time, causal structure, or a route with jumps and reversals. A corpus of linear stories cannot falsify our reorder machinery - every route looks the same when the source has only one. One deliberately anachronic, low-fame story is worth more to set 1 than a sixth linear one. Candidate worth scoring: Chesnutt, The Goophered Grapevine (The Conjure Woman, 1899) - embedded retrospective telling by a motivated narrator, which is also the retrospective-narrator stress case the chief wants from Araby, in a text far less summarized than Joyce.

Chief: this is docs-only on my own bead and reversible; revert or amend freely. The two decisions I would like from you when convenient - (a) whether the contamination rule stays a manifest selection rule or becomes a protocol law (protocol revision + the one-line ProtocolDocument.pinned bump in embed-bench, landed together); (b) whether to add an anachrony slot to set 1, which changes the story count and therefore the recall panel arithmetic in the doc.
